questions.scenario: On Mar 1 Masco opens an LC at City Bank: USD 25,000 yarn purchase from ABC Yarn, with ৳3,10,000 cash margin deposited and ৳15,500 LC opening commission charged to the bank account. Which entry records the OPENING event?
options: Dr Inventory—Yarn 31,00,000 / Cr Accounts Payable—ABC Yarn 31,00,000
Dr LC Margin Deposit 3,10,000 + Dr LC Commission Expense 15,500 / Cr Cash at Bank—City Bank 3,25,500
Dr Accounts Payable—ABC Yarn 3,25,500 / Cr Cash at Bank 3,25,500
No entry — the LC is only a promise until yarn arrives
questions.explanation: Opening an LC moves cash (margin) and charges a fee (commission expense); yarn itself has not yet arrived, so Inventory and Accounts Payable stay at zero. The actual purchase is recorded when the GRN is created (Module 7).
wrongExplanations: That is the GRN entry — posted 9 days later when yarn physically arrived.
The margin and commission are not a payment to ABC Yarn; they leave the bank but are owed to no supplier yet.
Opening has real cash effects today (margin moves, commission charged) — it must be journalized, even though no yarn has been received.

questions.scenario: GRN-2026-0287 (Mar 10) shows a full 5,000 kg yarn receipt from ABC Yarn at ৳31,00,000. Which document is the source for the Dr Inventory—Yarn / Cr Accounts Payable—ABC Yarn entry?
options: The LC opening advice
The bank payment voucher
The Goods Receipt Note (GRN), backed by the supplier invoice and B/L
The production output report
questions.explanation: The GRN is the event record (yarn physically received), supported by the supplier invoice (price) and B/L (proof of shipment). The LC opening is a promise, not a receipt; the payment voucher is a later event; the production report belongs to a different event entirely (Module 4).
wrongExplanations: LC opening records cash out — it does not prove inventory arrival.
Payment records cash leaving the bank to settle an earlier payable, not a new receipt.
Production output moves cost between WIP and Finished Goods — no supplier involved.

questions.scenario: On Mar 15 ABC Yarn submits invoice INV-0991 for the same 5,000 kg yarn already covered by INV-0987. Commercial officer Nasrin spots it. What should the system have done BEFORE paying?
options: Auto-pay all matching amounts
Reject the second invoice — the supplier already has a posted payable for this shipment; pay nothing extra
Pay both and let the auditor catch it later
Pay half and call it a discount
questions.explanation: A duplicate invoice for a shipment already posted creates a phantom payable of ৳31,00,000. The control is three-way matching (PO + GRN + Invoice) BEFORE payment (Module 9 + Module 12). Nasrin's catch saves a real ৳31 lakh loss — paying a duplicate, even by accident, is often unrecoverable.
wrongExplanations: Auto-pay with no matching is how real money disappears from factories every year.
Auditors find what is already gone — not a substitute for prevention.
A 50% payment has no contractual basis and may be flagged as partial/abusive by the supplier.

questions.scenario: On Mar 12 XYZ Mills delivers only 2,500 kg out of 3,000 kg invoiced (৳18,60,000). Which entry is NOT yet justified at month-end?
options: Dr Inventory—Yarn 15,50,000 / Cr Accounts Payable—XYZ Mills 15,50,000
Dr Inventory—Yarn 18,60,000 / Cr Accounts Payable—XYZ Mills 18,60,000 — paying the full invoice
A written query note to XYZ Mills for the 500 kg short shipment
Marking the GRN as 'PARTIAL — 500 kg short'
questions.explanation: Posting the full ৳18,60,000 to inventory records yarn we never received. Per Module 13, book what you can prove (2,500 kg = ৳15,50,000), query the short shipment, and adjust later when the missing 500 kg arrives or the claim is settled. Paying the full invoice would be worse still: paying for goods not in the warehouse.
wrongExplanations: Books the receipt for the 2,500 kg we can actually count — defensible and conservative.
The query note IS the right action; Module 13 calls this a supplier discrepancy note.
Marking partial on the GRN is the source-document annotation that lets finance book conservatively.

questions.scenario: A 3,000 kg yarn delivery from XYZ Mills has NO GRN in the system, even though Jamal's team logged it onto the receiving floor. What entry is appropriate today?
options: Dr Inventory—Yarn 18,60,000 / Cr Accounts Payable—XYZ Mills 18,60,000
No accounting entry; raise a query to Jamal to investigate why the GRN was never created
Dr Inventory—Yarn 18,60,000 / Cr Suspense 18,60,000
Dr Wastage Expense 18,60,000 / Cr Accounts Payable—XYZ Mills 18,60,000
questions.explanation: No GRN means no event has been formally recorded (Module 4: documents are the source of truth). Until Jamal creates the GRN — accounting for any shortage — we cannot book the payable or inventory. Bookkeeping on a missing GRN is bookkeeping on rumor; the audit trail starts with the document (Module 12).
wrongExplanations: Posting without a GRN invents a source document; later reconciliation will fail.
Suspense is for KNOWN events with UNCLEAR accounts — this is an UNKNOWN event.
Wastage is a controlled category, not a default for unrecorded receipts.

questions.scenario: On Mar 20 Masco ships 15,000 pcs to H&M under B/L-EXP-2026-0034. Revenue is recognized on the B/L DATE, not when H&M pays. Which entries record this event at shipment?
options: Dr Cash at Bank 63,75,000 / Cr Sales Revenue 63,75,000
Dr Accounts Receivable—H&M 63,75,000 / Cr Sales Revenue 63,75,000; Dr COGS 38,00,000 / Cr Finished Goods Inventory 38,00,000
Dr Accounts Receivable—H&M 63,75,000 / Cr Accounts Payable 63,75,000
No entry — wait until H&M's bank pays via LC
questions.explanation: The B/L date is the revenue-recognition trigger (Module 7 + Module 11). At shipment: book the receivable + revenue AND the cost-of-goods-sold + finished goods reduction. Two entries, two events — performance obligation satisfied (control passed to H&M), inventory physically gone.
wrongExplanations: Cash has not moved; LC settlement is weeks later. Premature cash recognition is the very error Module 7 warns against.
That treats H&M as a supplier, not a customer — signs swapped.
Waiting for cash violates accrual accounting (Module 0/11) and would let management shift revenue between periods by delaying B/L release.

questions.scenario: Payroll for March: gross salaries ৳18,00,000, TDS withheld ৳90,000, net bank-paid ৳17,10,000. Which three-line entry records this event?
options: Dr Salaries Expense 18,00,000 / Cr TDS Payable 90,000 + Cr Cash at Bank 17,10,000
Dr Salaries Expense 17,10,000 / Cr Cash at Bank 17,10,000
Dr Salaries Expense 18,00,000 / Cr Cash at Bank 18,00,000 — TDS is a separate later entry
Dr Cash at Bank 17,10,000 / Cr Salaries Expense 17,10,000
questions.explanation: Total expense is ৳18,00,000 (the full cost to Masco). Cash leaving the bank is only ৳17,10,000. The missing ৳90,000 is held back as TDS — owed to NBR, not paid to employees (Module 8 + Module 14). Two credits, one debit, balanced.
wrongExplanations: This understates expense by ৳90,000 and hides a real liability to NBR.
Treating TDS as a later event violates matching — the obligation exists at payment time.
Backwards: that says Masco RECEIVED money from salaries, not paid them.

questions.scenario: The trial balance at March 31 ties perfectly (debits = credits to the paisa). Two months later an internal auditor finds a duplicate payment of ৳31,00,000 to ABC Yarn that went out because the duplicate invoice was paid in April. How is this possible?
options: Balanced is not the same as correct: the trial balance catches arithmetic asymmetry, not duplicate payments where both entries balance
Balanced proves everything is correct — the auditor must be mistaken
Trial balances only work at year-end
A duplicate payment cannot balance; the system would have refused it
questions.explanation: Balanced means only Σdebits = Σcredits (Module 1). Duplicate balanced entries (same amount both sides, posted twice with matching offset) STILL balance. This is exactly the class of error the trial balance cannot detect — three-way matching (PO+GRN+Invoice) and supplier reconciliations are the real defense (Modules 9, 12).
wrongExplanations: Balanced is an arithmetic check, not a truth check; the Module 1 lesson warned explicitly about this.
Trial balances matter every close — month-end for early error detection.
Duplicate entries DO balance: Dr Cash 31L / Cr AP 31L posted twice leaves the system balanced, just twice wrong.

questions.scenario: Masco's March mini income statement shows Revenue ৳63,75,000, COGS ৳38,00,000, salaries ৳18,00,000, depreciation ৳2,50,000, LC commission ৳15,500, electricity ৳4,50,000 (paid 3,50,000 + March accrual 50,000 + reclassified correction 50,000). What is the net profit?
options: Negative ৳2,40,500
Zero — profit cancels with depreciation
wrongExplanations: That is gross sales — expenses have not been subtracted.
That would be true only if expenses were ৳28,15,500 — they are ৳24,15,500.
Depreciation is an expense, not a profit cancellation.

questions.scenario: March's net profit is ৳59,500 but the bank account fell by several lakhs during the month (LC margin, salaries, electricity, supplier payments all in cash; no LC settlement arrived yet from H&M). Why does profit differ from cash movement?
options: Profit and cash must always match — the books are wrong

Accrual vs cash timing: profit includes revenue earned but not yet collected (AR—H&M) and excludes cash spent on items not yet expensed (inventory still on the balance sheet). Cash trails profit until receivables are realized.
The bank must be misreporting
Profit is always higher than cash movement
questions.explanation: Accrual accounting (Modules 0, 11) recognizes revenue when earned and expense when incurred — not when cash moves. We booked ৳63,75,000 revenue at B/L date but H&M's bank has not yet paid; meanwhile we paid ৳17,10,000 cash for salaries (expensed) and ৳18,60,000-ish for yarn (sitting in Inventory, not yet expensed). Profit is a performance measure; cash is a liquidity measure — both true, but rarely equal in any single month.
wrongExplanations: Accrual systems intentionally separate the two; the difference is the working-capital story.
Banks don't misreport large systematic gaps over a full month — the divergence is structural.
Profit can be higher OR lower than cash movement depending on receivables, payables, and inventory build-up.

questions.scenario: An end-of-March supplier statement from ABC Yarn shows an outstanding balance of ৳27,90,000. Masco's books show a ৳3,10,000 credit balance in ABC Yarn's account (i.e., ABC Yarn owes us the uncollected return credit). The gap equals one item. What is it?
options: A timing difference on bank payment
The duplicate invoice INV-0991 (৳31,00,000), which Masco correctly never posted; ABC Yarn's own statement still includes it, so their ৳27,90,000 is overstated by exactly ৳31,00,000
Unrecorded depreciation
Unrecorded TDS on salaries
questions.explanation: ABC Yarn's statement: 31,00,000 (INV-0987) + 31,00,000 (INV-0991 duplicate) − 3,10,000 (RET-0008) − 31,00,000 (PAY) = ৳27,90,000. Masco's books: 31,00,000 (INV-0987) − 3,10,000 (RET-0008) − 31,00,000 (PAY) = −৳3,10,000 (a credit in Masco's favour, the uncollected return credit). The ৳31,00,000 gap between the two positions equals the duplicate INV-0991, which Masco correctly rejected. Once ABC Yarn removes INV-0991 from their statement, their position becomes −৳3,10,000, exactly matching ours. The ৳3,10,000 credit appears on Masco's closing balance sheet as 'Receivable from ABC Yarn ৳3,10,000' under assets. No journal adjustment is needed in Masco's books — but the supplier must be told in writing so they do not 'age' the supposed debt (Module 9).
wrongExplanations: Payment timing was already matched via the bank payment voucher (BPV-0351); the gap is not a clearing-date issue.
Depreciation never appears on a supplier statement.
Salary TDS is between Masco and NBR, not between Masco and ABC Yarn.
